title: Bring in a second clip and cut between clips
goal: There is no way to bring a second recording into a video document, so every edit happens inside one clip. Let a person drop another video or a sound onto the timeline at the moment and on the track they point at, and cut between clips.
notes:

Multi-clip editing was never filed. Target: the user's mocks (docs/design/mocks/pages/video.html, video-shell.html, comp-video.html and the page named here) at their fidelity; runner-prompt rules on default config, side-by-side with the mock, labels-not-explanations and right-click apply. pre-build review: (1) A second recording CAN already land today, but only by letting go over the picture: at the playhead, on top, on a track of its own. The timeline takes no drop, so a Premiere editor dragging b-roll to a spot on V1 gets nothing. (2) Premiere's default drag is overwrite and Cmd-drag is insert; that is what ships here, read off the held keys since a drop carries none. (3) Clips on one track may not overlap (canPlace), so overwrite has to trim, split or remove what it lands on, and a split of a clip across the landing has to become TWO layers because a clip's pieces cannot hold a hole. (4) A sound let go over a picture track has nowhere to go on that track; Premiere puts it on the matching audio track, so it lands on the first unlocked sound track, or a new one, at the moment under the pointer, and the ghost is drawn where it really lands. (5) Mock assumption the app cannot deliver: the Library's Media shelf holds pictures only, so 'drag b-roll.mov off the Library' has no tile to drag. Filing that as its own p1. (6) 'Each clip keeps its own sound as a segment under it' is exactly task a-clip-s-sound-is-on-the-timeline-from-the-momen (next in line): here the sound rides with the clip and moves, trims and splits with it; the separate segment is that task's.

left rough (no task earned): the lanes shrink once when a file arrives because the timeline makes room past its end for it; an insert does not preview later clips moving; a picked edit point clears the layer pick but leaves the picked track's properties in the panel (edit point properties are the transition task's).

A video or sound let go on the timeline lands at the moment and on the track under the pointer: overwrite by default (trim/split into two layers/remove), insert with Command (split + push along), sound retargeted to a sound track, snapping, a dashed ghost while in the air with room past the end, edit points between butted clips (comp-video 02), clips alternating the mock's two colours; a drop over the picture still lands at the playhead.
